result.topic_en: Notes on transformation formulas for the hypergeometric series $F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,x)$ (quadratic transformations), integral representations with substitutions, and a recursive/series computation for a confluent-type integral involving $e^{-y}y^{\alpha-1}(1-xy)^{-\beta}$.
result.transcription:
$F(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,x) = F(\alpha+1,-\gamma,\alpha+\beta+2,x)$ \quad $\alpha,\beta,-\frac12-\beta,\frac32-\alpha$
$F(\alpha-1,\gamma-\alpha-1,-\beta,x) = F(\alpha,\beta,\beta,x)$
$F(\alpha-1,\beta-\frac12,-\beta,x) = F\left(2\alpha-1,\beta-\alpha-\frac12,\beta-\alpha-\frac12,\frac{\sqrt{1-x}-1}{\sqrt{1-x}-1}\right)\;-2\beta$
$F(\alpha,\beta,-\frac12-\beta,x) = F(2\alpha+1,\beta-\alpha-1,\beta-\alpha-1,\quad)$
$F(\alpha-1,\beta-\frac12,-\beta,x) = F\left(2\alpha-1,2\beta-1,-\alpha-\beta,\frac{\pm2\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{x-1}\pm\sqrt{x}}\right)\;-\alpha-\beta$
$F(\alpha-1,\beta-\frac12,-\beta,x) = F\left(2\alpha-1,\beta-\alpha-\frac12,-2\beta,\frac{1-\sqrt{1-x}}{2}\right)\;\beta-\alpha-\frac12$
$F(\alpha-1,\gamma-\alpha-1,-\alpha-\frac12\gamma[?])$
$-\beta\quad F(\alpha-1,2\beta-\alpha-1,-\beta,x) = F\left(\alpha-1,\alpha-2\beta,\beta-\alpha-\frac12,\left(\frac{1-\sqrt{1-x}}{1+\sqrt{1-x}}\right)^2\right)\;\beta-\alpha-\frac12$
$F(\alpha-1,-\beta,-\beta,x) = (1+x)^{-\alpha}F\left(\frac{\alpha}{2}-1,\frac{\alpha}{2}-\beta,-\frac{\alpha+1}{2},\frac{4x}{(1+x)^2}\right)$
$\int y^{\alpha-1}(1-y)^{-\beta}(1-xy)^{-\beta}\partial y \quad (1+x)^{-\alpha}\int z^{\frac{\alpha}{2}-1}(1-z)^{\frac{\alpha}{2}-\beta}\left(1-\frac{4xz}{(1+x)^2}\right)^{-\frac{\alpha}{2}+\frac12}\partial z = [-\int z^{\frac{\alpha}{2}-\frac12}(1-z)-]$
$\frac{z(1-z)}{(1+x)^2-4xz} = y^2$
$1-(1+x)y+xy^2 = 1-z$
$y(1-x(1-y)) = z-1$
$\frac{(1+x)^2}{4x}-(1+x)y+xy^2 = \frac{1+x^2}{4x}-z$
$(1+x)^2-4x(1+x)y+4x^2y^2$

$\frac{1}{1-xy} = z \quad xy = [-\ldots-]\;\frac{z-1}{z}$
$\frac{\partial y}{x} = -\frac{\partial z}{x^2z^2}$
$\gamma=\infty \quad$
$p_n = (\alpha+n)x \quad q_n = (\beta+n)x$

$a'_{n+1}+a'_n = b'_n$

$\sum_{0,\infty}b'_n\zeta^n = v = \sum_{0,\infty}(a'_{n+1}+a'_n)\zeta^n = a'_0+\sum_{0,\infty}a'_{n+1}\zeta^n(1+\zeta)$
$\frac{v}{(1+\zeta)x} = \frac{a'_0}{x(1+\zeta)}+\sum_{0,\infty}((\beta+n+1)b'_{n+1}+(\alpha+n)b'_n)\zeta^n$

methods.what: Quadratic transformation of the hypergeometric series with argument $4x/(1+x)^2$
Euler-type integral and substitution relating $y$ and $z$ for the quadratic transformation
Recurrences for numerators and denominators of a continued fraction (case $\gamma=\infty$)
Generating function of normalized recurrence coefficients leading to a differential equation for $v$
Integrating the differential equation via exact differential with factor $e^{-y}y^\alpha(1-xy)^{-\beta}$
